skill.name: event-sourcing-architect
skill.description: Design event sourced systems with CQRS, event stores, projections, sagas, snapshots, and versioned events for reliable audit trails.
skill.summary: Plan event sourced architectures with clear streams, projections, sagas, and evolution strategies.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Event sourced systems are hard to design because streams, projections, and consistency rules must align. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code plan CQRS architectures with practical tradeoffs.
actual_capabilities: Identifies aggregate boundaries and event streams for event sourced domains.
Designs immutable domain events, command handlers, and event application flows.
Plans projections and read models for CQRS query requirements.
Defines saga and process manager patterns for cross-aggregate workflows.
Recommends snapshotting, versioning, and replay strategies for long-lived systems.
limitations: It does not replace environment-specific architecture review or production testing.
It is not suitable for simple CRUD systems where event sourcing adds needless complexity.
It cannot validate live infrastructure, event store capacity, or runtime performance.
It assumes teams can operate projections, replays, and eventual consistency.

use_cases.title: Model Audit-Heavy Domains
use_cases.description: Design event streams and immutable events for systems that need reliable history and temporal queries.

use_cases.title: Plan CQRS Read Models
use_cases.description: Separate write models from query models and define projections for reporting, dashboards, and search.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Distributed Workflows
use_cases.description: Map sagas, compensating actions, and idempotent handlers for multi-step business processes.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Fit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this product requirement and tell me if event sourcing is appropriate. Explain the tradeoffs, risks, and simpler alternatives.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before committing to event sourcing.

prompt_templates.title: Design Aggregates
prompt_templates.prompt: Given this domain workflow, identify aggregate boundaries, commands, events, and event streams. Highlight consistency boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Projections
prompt_templates.prompt: Design CQRS read models for these query requirements. Include projection sources, rebuild strategy, idempotency, and lag handling.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when planning user-facing reads and reports.

prompt_templates.title: Review Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this event sourced architecture for stream design, event versioning, saga orchestration, snapshotting, and operational failure modes.

output_examples.input: Design an order workflow with payment, fulfillment, and cancellation.
output_examples.output: A response that defines order, payment, and shipment streams, key events, command handlers, saga steps, and compensating actions.

output_examples.input: Plan read models for customer account history and balance views.
output_examples.output: A response that lists projection responsibilities, rebuild order, idempotency rules, consistency expectations, and stale-data handling.

output_examples.input: Review our event versioning approach before release.
output_examples.output: A response that checks backward compatibility, upcasting needs, migration risks, replay safety, and consumer rollout sequencing.

best_practices: Start with domain events as immutable facts, then derive commands, projections, and workflows.
Define replay, rebuild, and versioning strategies before the first production release.
Use idempotent handlers and correlation identifiers for reliable processing and traceability.
anti_patterns: Do not use event sourcing only because it sounds modern.
Do not mutate or delete committed production events as a normal workflow.
Do not hide cross-aggregate consistency needs inside synchronous command handlers.

faq.question: Does this skill generate production code?
faq.answer: It focuses on architecture guidance and design review. Any generated implementation should be tested in your environment.

faq.question: Can it help decide if event sourcing is needed?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare event sourcing with simpler CRUD and transactional approaches for a given domain.

faq.question: Does it cover CQRS?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps separate command models from read models and plan projection behavior.

faq.question: Can it design sagas?
faq.answer: Yes. It can map process managers, compensating actions, and retry boundaries for distributed workflows.

faq.question: Does it handle event versioning?
faq.answer: Yes. It can recommend versioning, upcasting, and rollout strategies for changing event schemas.

faq.question: Is it safe for simple applications?
faq.answer: It can advise against event sourcing when CRUD, transactions, or simpler audit logs are enough.
